references.text: Joshua reminds the people that the Lord will give them rest from all their enemies and a land to live in, fulfilling the promise in Deuteronomy.
The Lord gave Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and all the promises were fulfilled as they settled in the land.
The Lord had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, fulfilling the promise of peace and security.
The Lord gave David rest from all his enemies around him, a parallel to the promise of rest in the promised land.
Solomon describes how the Lord has given rest on every side, with no enemies or disaster, as the fulfillment of the promise.
The command to cross the Jordan and take possession of the land as an inheritance, which is the basis for the promise in Deuteronomy 12:10.
Moses speaks of how the Lord will give their brothers rest and that they shall take possession of the land on the other side of the Jordan.
When the Lord gives rest from all enemies around them in the land, Israel is to blot out the memory of Amalek.
The book of Hebrews interprets the promise of rest as something greater than just the physical land, pointing toward a spiritual Sabbath rest for God's people.
